items.headline: Sentiment rebounds sharply while valuation remains extreme
items.summary: The live AGCI engine moved to Greed 78/100, up 19 points in one day, while Valuation remains 88/100. The matrix returned to PRICE_DISCIPLINE. Barron's Review & Preview noted the equity rally after the Fed hike.
items.whyItMatters: The rebound removes the prior HOLD_ANALYZE setup before valuation has reset. Avoid interpreting post-Fed strength as a broad margin-of-safety signal; preserve liquidity and price discipline.

items.headline: BOJ raises policy rate to 1.25% but yen weakens
items.summary: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, and signaled willingness to tighten further. The 7-2 vote and less-hawkish-than-expected communication nevertheless pushed the yen lower rather than higher.
items.whyItMatters: Japan has entered a more preemptive inflation-fighting phase, but the FX reaction shows positioning and guidance matter as much as the hike. Review JPY hedges and global carry exposure rather than assuming automatic yen appreciation.

items.headline: Oil eases but stagflation risk remains elevated
items.summary: Brent eased toward roughly $104 as Saudi rerouting via Oman, higher product inventories and Chinese fuel exports reduced immediate scarcity fears. Physical Middle East risk remains unresolved, and Reuters notes the combination of energy costs and elevated global yields is increasing stagflation risk.
items.whyItMatters: The correct portfolio response remains a moderate energy hedge without chasing crude. High oil plus high sovereign yields raises discount rates and pressure on consumers, housing and long-duration assets even if spot crude retreats.

items.headline: AI infrastructure demand remains visible despite valuation and governance risk
items.summary: GlobalFoundries and Marvell expanded capacity collaboration for high-speed AI data-center connectivity, while SK Hynix's Solidigm is evaluating a U.S. NAND fab. Barron's Daily Roundup also highlighted continued AI-driven demand around SpaceX.
items.whyItMatters: Physical supply-chain commitments support the view that AI infrastructure demand has not disappeared. Underwriting should still require funded demand, utilization, power, margins, free cash flow and governance rather than extrapolating sector-wide multiples.
